title: Applying Advanced In Vitro Culturing Technology to Study the Human Gut Microbiota
protocol: Prepare the defined medium by filling a 4 L flask with 2 L of double distilled, deionized water.
Add 29.2 g of defined medium powder to the water and mix until fully homogenized.
Autoclave the mixture at 121 °C for 30 min.
After cooling, store the prepared defined medium in a refrigerator at 4 °C with constant agitation using a magnetic stirrer.
Prepare pancreatic juice by autoclaving 2 L of distilled, deionized water in a 5 L vessel with a stirrer bar added at 121 °C for 30 min.
Allow the autoclaved water to cool to room temperature.
Add 12.5 g NaHCO3, 6 g bile, and 0.9 g pancreatin.
Place on magnetic stirrer to mix thoroughly.
Store the prepared pancreatic juice in a refrigerator at 4 °C with agitation until ready for use (maximum of 2-3 days).
Prepare phosphate buffer by adding 0.5 L of distilled, deionized water to a 1 L flask containing a magnetic stirrer bar and turning on agitation.
Add 6.8 g KH2PO4, 8.8 g K2HPO4, and 0.1 g sodium thioglycolate.
Top off with water to a final volume of 1 L after the components have completely dissolved.
Adjust the pH to 7.0 using NaOH.
Pour 2 L of buffer into a vessel with a screw cap lid.
Autoclave the buffer at 121 °C for 30 min with the lid screwed on loosely.
Allow the autoclaved buffer to cool to room temperature.
Store the buffer at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
Autoclave plastic mucin carriers, forceps, plastic mesh, and zip ties at 131 °C for 30 min.
Autoclave 300 mL of double distilled, de-ionized water at 131 °C for 30 min.
Fill sterile Petri dishes with the plastic mucin carriers using sterile forceps in a biosafety cabinet.
Add 3 g of bacterial agar and 15 g of porcine mucin to 300 mL of autoclaved water.
Boil the solution containing bacterial agar and porcine mucin.
Cool the boiled solution for 1 min.
Repeat boiling and cooling for a total of three times.
Pour cooled liquid mucin agar over plastic mucin carriers in Petri dishes.
Place the lid back on the Petri dish.
Allow the Petri dish to cool under laminar flow.
Take autoclaved plastic netting using sterile forceps.
Insert mucin carriers containing solidified mucin agar into the netting.
Close the ends of the mesh with zip ties.
Store the assembled net at 4°C until use.
Place 10 bioreactors containing stirrer bars on magnetic stirrers.
Turn on agitation for the bioreactors.
Connect 5 bioreactors in sequence using silicon tubing and peristaltic pump.
Label the bioreactors as Stomach, small intestine, ascending colon, transverse colon, descending colon.
Place the defined medium and pancreatic juice in a refrigerator at 4 °C with constant agitation using magnetic stirrers.
Connect the defined medium to the stomach bioreactor via silicon tubing and peristaltic pump.
Connect the pancreatic juice to the small intestine via silicon tubing and peristaltic pump.
Add solidifying agent to a urine drainage bag.
Connect the descending colon to the urine drainage bag by way of the peristaltic pump.
Dispose of the solidified waste as biological waste during the experiment.
Using silicone tubing, connect the water jacket of each vessel in order.
Connect each end of the vessels' water jackets to the circulating water bath.
Fill the circulating water bath with distilled water and set to 37 °C.
Connect acid and base to each vessel lid using peristaltic pumps.
Insert pH probes into each vessel through designated ports in the lid.
Set stomach pH to 2.
Set small intestine pH to 6.7-6.9.
Set ascending colon pH to 5.6-5.9.
Set transverse colon pH to 6.15-6.4.
Set descending colon pH to 6.6-6.9.
Connect a nitrogen line to the lid of each vessel using designated ports.
Ensure each unit has its own flush for preventing cross contamination.
Insert a metal sample tube through the lid of each bioreactor using designated ports.
Add a small piece of silicon tubing to the top end of the sample tube.
Connect a Luer Lock to the top end of the sample tube.
Fill the ascending colon region with 500 mL of defined medium.
Fill the transverse colon region with 800 mL of defined medium.
Fill the descending colon region with 600 mL of defined medium.
Add mucin agar carriers to each colon region, proportional to the volume of the reactor.
Remove excess defined medium using a syringe and sample tube after adding the carriers.
Turn on pH probes in each reactor for pH adjustment.
Turn on nitrogen flush for 20 minutes.
Thaw fecal homogenate following manufacturer’s guidelines prior to inoculation.
Inoculate the ascending colon reactor with 25 mL of fecal homogenate through the sample port using a syringe.
Inoculate the transverse colon reactor with 40 mL of fecal homogenate through the sample port using a syringe.
Inoculate the descending colon reactor with 30 mL of fecal homogenate through the sample port using a syringe.
Grow the cultures in the bioreactors overnight with pH control.
Harvest samples of the luminal fluid from each colon region after overnight growth.
Turn on the computer program to begin feeding.
Pump 140 mL of defined medium into the stomach bioreactor three times a day and allow it to incubate for 1 h.
Pump the contents of the stomach into the small intestine after 1 h.
Pump 60 mL of pancreatic juice into the small intestine simultaneously with pumping stomach contents.
Adjust pH in the small intestine to pH 6.7-6.9 during incubation.
Turn on nitrogen flush for each system for a total of 10 min each during incubation.
Allow the mixture in the small intestine to incubate for 90 mins.
Turn on pumps from the small intestine to the ascending colon after the 90 min incubation.
Pump contents from the ascending colon to the transverse colon simultaneously.
Pump contents from the transverse colon to the descending colon simultaneously.
Pump contents from the descending colon to the waste simultaneously.
Harvest samples from overnight growth following the protocol below.
Begin daily cycles, feeding three times a day following the protocol above.
Run the experiment for a total of 2 weeks to allow bacteria to stabilize.
Maintain pH during system running.
Follow daily feeding cycles three times a day.
Change mucosal carriers 2-3 times each week.
After stabilization, run the experiment for 2 weeks as control period.
Use the system to test different components or variables after control period.
Stop adding components or variables and return conditions to normal after treatment period.
Consider wash-out period to determine if changes to community are permanent.
Clean Luer Lock on sample port with either 70% ethanol or small alcohol pad.
Allow Luer Lock to dry completely.
Ensure all air is removed from a 30 mL syringe.
Connect 30 mL syringe to the sample port.
Draw up and down 3-5 times to ensure proper mixing of vessel components.
Draw a total of 30 mL of culture.
Aliquot luminal samples into sterile falcon tubes and store on ice.
Transfer stored samples to a -80°C freezer after sampling is completed.
Spin 15 mL of the luminal sample at 4°C, 5,000 x g for 10 min for SCFA analysis.
Syringe filter the supernatant using a PES 0.2 μm filter.
Store the filtered supernatant at -80°C.
Spin 1 mL of luminal fluid at 4°C, 5,000 x g for 10 min for DNA analysis.
Discard the supernatant and store the pellet at -80°C.
Store 10 mL of luminal fluid at -80°C as a backup.
Remove and bring out prepared mucin carriers from the refrigerator.
Turn on nitrogen flush and open reactor lid quickly.
Remove 50% of mucin carriers and add new ones.
Seal the lid quickly and keep nitrogen flush on for another 20 min.
Aliquot 0.25-0.5 g of agar into a 2 mL tube for DNA extraction.
Store the agar aliquots at -80°C until needed.
Prepare CTAB buffer by dissolving K2HPO4 and NaCl in deionized, distilled water.
Autoclave the solution at 121°C for 30 min.
Allow the solution to cool to room temperature.
Add Hexadecyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) and heat to 60°C with agitation.
After all the CTAB is dissolved, remove the solution from heat and cool to room temperature.
Dissolve 300 g of polyethylene glycol 6,000 and 93.5 g NaCl in 1 L of deionized, distilled water.
Autoclave the PEG-6000 solution at 121 °C for 30 min.
Cool the autoclaved solution to room temperature before use.
Add 500 μL of CTAB buffer and 500 μL of Phenol-Chloroform-Isoamyl alcohol to a 2 mL sample tube.
Vortex the sample tube to homogenize its contents.
Transfer the entire contents of the sample tube to a 0.1 mm physical homogenizing tube.
Homogenize the tubes for 20 s at the highest setting two times, with a 20 s pause in between.
Centrifuge the homogenized tubes at 3,000 x g for 5 mins.
Transfer 300 μL of the supernatant to a clean, 1.7 mL tube and add 500 μL of CTAB buffer to the original tube.
Homogenize this tube again using the methods in steps 4.3.2-4.3.3 and centrifuge at 3,000 x g for 5 min.
After centrifugation, transfer another 300 μL of supernatant to the new tube which now contains 600 μL.
Add a total of 600 μL Chloroform-Isoamyl alcohol to the tube containing 600 μL of the supernatant.
Invert the tubes to mix, and then centrifuge briefly.
Transfer 500 μL of the upper phase to a clean 1.7 mL tube.
Ensure only to take the top phase.
Add 1000 μL of Peg-6000 solution to the tubes.
Invert the tubes to mix.
Incubate at room temperature for 2 h.
Centrifuge the tubes at 18,200 x g, 4 °C, for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Clean the pellet with ice cold 70% ethanol.
Centrifuge the tubes again at 18,200 x g, 4 °C, for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Allow the pellet to dry in the biosafety cabinet under laminar flow.
Add 75 μL of RNAse free, DNAse free, sterile water to each tube.
Quantify the resuspended DNA by a spectrophotometer.
Thaw the frozen samples at 40°C for 30 min.
Extract short chain fatty acids using diethyl ether in a 2:1 (v:v) ratio.
Transfer the organic phase to a GC/MS equipped with a column, 30 m, 0.25 mm ID, 0.25 µm.
Inject 10 μL of sample into the GC/MS.
Set the injection port temperature to 260 °C and initial column temperature to 125 °C.
Hold the initial temperature for 1 min.
Increase the column temperature to 250 °C over 11.5 min with a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Quantify the amount of each SCFA using standard curves and 2-methylhexanoic acid as the internal standard.
